content.title: About
content.content: Pork cured as bacon, pre‑cooked and ready for restaurant service. Smoking gives the meat its distinctive aroma, while heat treatment makes it safe and tender. This type of bacon is commonly used in hot dishes, salads and appetizers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Smoking meat is an ancient preservation method that also adds flavor.
Pork bacon contains more fat than most other bacon types, making it especially juicy.
In restaurants bacon is often crisped, but this product is already cooked and can be served without further heating.
There are several smoking methods: cold smoking (up to 30 °C) and hot smoking (70 °C and above). Restaurant bacon is usually hot‑smoked.
Pork provides all essential amino acids as a complete protein source.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Bacon supplies high‑quality animal protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc aids immune function and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The fat in bacon provides a concentrated source of energy, useful during high physical activity.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Smoked bacon often contains a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: A high amount of saturated fat may contribute to cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Potential carcinogens
items.content: Smoking creates compounds such as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, which are considered potential carcinogens in large amounts.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to pork proteins.

items.title: Not suitable for certain diets
items.content: Those on low‑fat or low‑salt diets should limit bacon intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ready‑to‑eat bacon can be added to hot dishes, tossed into salads, used in sandwiches, or served as a side to vegetables. For extra crunch, briefly sear it before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bacon refrigerated at 0–4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container for up to 5 days. For longer storage freeze at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 3 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
